title: Marked mapping complexes are full unions of components
statement:
Use fully scaled categorical patterns and their fibered marked objects from [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], marked simplicial sets, flat and sharp markings and coordinatewise product markings from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], and Kan complexes from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $\mathfrak P=(C,S,\{p_\alpha\})$ be a small such pattern, let $W=(W,M)\to\bar C=(C,S)$ be any marked object, and let $Z\to\bar C$ be $\mathfrak P$-fibered. Define
$$K_Z=\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(W^\flat,Z),\qquad \operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(A,Z)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{/\bar C}(A\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Z).$$
Then $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(W,Z)\hookrightarrow K_Z$ is the full simplicial subset on those vertices $h:W\to Z$ carrying every edge of $M$ to a marked edge of $Z$. This full subset is a union of connected components of the Kan complex $K_Z$: if one vertex in a component preserves the marking, every vertex in that component does, and the subset contains every simplex with vertices in those components. This description is natural for postcomposition by marked maps between fibered objects. The empty domain and components with no marking-preserving vertices are allowed.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Lemma B.2.4(a), printed pp.1483-1484: full simplicial subset description of sharp marked mapping complexes; its union-of-components refinement. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical fact.

proof.text: Put $L=\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_C(W,Z)$ and $K=K_Z$. The identity on the underlying simplicial set gives a marked map $i:W^\flat\to W$ over $\bar C$, since every degenerate edge lies in $M$. By the product markings of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model], restriction $r:L\to K$ only forgets conditions on marked edges: its degree-$n$ map is inclusion of a subset of the same set of underlying maps $W\times\Delta^n\to Z$ over $C$. It is therefore degreewise injective. In degree zero, $W\times\Delta^0=W$ with precisely the original marking, so $L_0$ consists exactly of the marking-preserving vertex diagrams stated in the item.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4(a), printed pp.1483-1484; definitional identification of the vertical inclusion.

proof.text: The marked map $i$ is degreewise injective on underlying simplices: its underlying map is the identity. The target $Z$ is $\mathfrak P$-fibered by hypothesis. The final paragraph of [lem-coef-pattern-anodyne-lifting-products], applied to this $i$, consequently makes $r:L\to K$ a Kan fibration and makes both $L$ and $K$ Kan complexes. This uses restriction along an arbitrary degreewise injective marked map; it does not require $i$ to be pattern-anodyne or $W$ to be fibered.

source.place: Proposition B.1.14, printed pp.1481-1482, applied to the marking-enlargement cofibration.

proof.text: Use the horn-lifting meaning of Kan fibration in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. If an edge $a:\Delta^1\to K$ has either endpoint in $L_0$, that endpoint gives a map from the corresponding one-dimensional horn into $L$. Lifting this horn over $a$ produces an edge of $L$ whose image is exactly $a$. Its other endpoint therefore lies in $L_0$ as well. Both one-dimensional horns are available, so membership in $L_0$ is invariant under an edge traversed in either direction and under every finite edge zigzag. With connected components defined by the equivalence relation generated by endpoints of edges, the selected vertices are exactly a union of components of $K$.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4(a), printed pp.1483-1484; elementary component refinement using Proposition B.1.14.

proof.text: We prove fullness by induction on simplex dimension, using the horn characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For $n=0$ this is the definition of $L_0$. For $n=1$, an edge of $K$ whose vertices lie in $L_0$ lifts by Step 3 and thus belongs to $L_1$. For $n\geq2$, let $\sigma:\Delta^n\to K$ have all its vertices in $L_0$. Each $(n-1)$-face has this property and lies in $L$ by induction. Its lift is unique because $r$ is degreewise injective. These face lifts agree on every intersection, as their images agree there in $K$, so all faces except the zeroth glue to a map $\Lambda^n_0\to L$. Lift this horn against $r$ with bottom simplex $\sigma$. The resulting simplex of $L$ maps to $\sigma$, proving that $\sigma$ belongs to $L$. Conversely, all vertices of a simplex of $L$ belong to $L_0$ because $L$ is a simplicial subset. Thus $L$ is exactly the full simplicial subset spanned by $L_0$. Combined with Step 3, it is the asserted full union of components.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4(a), printed pp.1483-1484; explicit elementary horn induction supplying the full-subset claim.

proof.text: For a marked map $g:Z\to Z^{\prime}$ over $\bar C$, postcomposition sends a marked map $W\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to Z$ to a marked map into $Z^{\prime}$, by the definition of marked map in [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Forgetting the additional domain-marking conditions commutes strictly with this postcomposition in each degree. On vertices, a map carrying $M$ to marked edges still does so after composing with $g$. Hence the full-subset description is natural, including its component selection. If $W$ is empty, both mapping complexes have one simplex in every degree and $r$ is the identity. If there are no marking-preserving vertices, $L$ has no simplices, since every simplex has vertices; the same argument excludes exactly each unselected component. No nonemptiness or surjectivity hypothesis has been used.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4(a), printed pp.1483-1484; definitional postcomposition naturality and empty cases.

Step 2: the final paragraph of anodyne-lifting-products applies to W^flat->W with Z fibered, so r is a Kan fibration and L and K are Kan; this matches B.1.14, which needs only a cofibration. Face lifts are unique and glue to a map from the 0th horn, and the horn lift gives fullness. Step 5: naturality under postcomposition and the empty cases. Tested: W empty, M degenerate, Z empty, W=Delta^1 with its edge marked; naturality needs preservation only. No new nodes. lean.statement: theorem marked_mapping_components (P : CategoricalPattern.{u}) (W Z : Object P) (hZ : IsCategoricalPatternFibered P Z) : KanComplex (Marked.Over.mapSharp (Marked.Over.unmark ((toSharpSlice P).obj W)) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z)) ∧ (∀ n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ, Function.Injective ((Marked.Over.markingRestriction ((toSharpSlice P).obj W) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z)).app n)) ∧ Subcomplex.range (Marked.Over.markingRestriction ((toSharpSlice P).obj W) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z)) = fullSubcomplex (Marked.Over.mapSharp (Marked.Over.unmark ((toSharpSlice P).obj W)) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z)) (Marked.Over.PreservesSourceMarking ((toSharpSlice P).obj W) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z)) ∧ (∀ x y : (Marked.Over.mapSharp (Marked.Over.unmark ((toSharpSlice P).obj W)) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z)) _⦋0⦌, π₀.mk x = π₀.mk y → (Marked.Over.PreservesSourceMarking ((toSharpSlice P).obj W) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z) x ↔ Marked.Over.PreservesSourceMarking ((toSharpSlice P).obj W) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z) y)) ∧ (∀ (Z' : Object P), IsCategoricalPatternFibered P Z' → ∀ g : Z ⟶ Z', Marked.Over.markingRestriction ((toSharpSlice P).obj W) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z) ≫ Marked.Over.mapSharpPost (Marked.Over.unmark ((toSharpSlice P).obj W)) ((toSharpSlice P).map g) = Marked.Over.mapSharpPost ((toSharpSlice P).obj W) ((toSharpSlice P).map g) ≫ Marked.Over.markingRestriction ((toSharpSlice P).obj W) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z') ∧ ∀ x : (Marked.Over.mapSharp (Marked.Over.unmark ((toSharpSlice P).obj W)) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z)) _⦋0⦌, Marked.Over.PreservesSourceMarking ((toSharpSlice P).obj W) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z) x → Marked.Over.PreservesSourceMarking ((toSharpSlice P).obj W) ((toSharpSlice P).obj Z') ((Marked.Over.mapSharpPost (Marked.Over.unmark ((toSharpSlice P).obj W)) ((toSharpSlice P).map g)).app _ x))
